questions.question_text: A pattern has $10$ dots in each group and one group per stage. Which row completes stages $1$, $2$, $3$?

options.why: Adds $1$ dot per stage instead of adding another group of $10$.
Adds the stage number to $10$ instead of multiplying groups by dots per group.
Multiplies each previous count by $10$ instead of adding one equal group.

questions.question_text: A pattern has as many strips as its stage number, and each strip has $17$ tiles. What is the table entry for stage $4$?

options.why: Adds the stage number to $17$ instead of using four groups of $17$.
Uses only three groups of $17$, so the table is one stage behind.
Reverses the digits of the correct product rather than recording $4 \times 17$.

questions.question_text: A design has $19$ pegs per frame. Which pair belongs in the stage-$3$ column?

options.why: Adds $3$ to $19$ instead of counting three equal frames.
Counts only two frames of $19$, leaving the table one stage short.
Swaps the stage number and item count instead of keeping their roles.

questions.question_text: A $7$-section pattern contains $140$ beads. How many beads per section are used to build its table?

options.why: Adds the stage number to the bead count rather than finding one section.
Subtracts one stage number from the total rather than dividing into seven sections.
Multiplies the total by the stage number instead of dividing by it.

questions.question_text: A table for $21$ counters per group shows stage $2$ as $42$. What count should appear at stage $6$?

options.why: Adds four to $42$ for the stage gap instead of using six full groups.
Adds another $42$ once, which gives stage $4$ rather than stage $6$.
Multiplies the stage-$2$ count by $6$ instead of scaling it by $6 \div 2$.

questions.question_text: Which entry is wrong for a pattern with $22$ lights per panel: $\begin{array}{c|cccc}\text{Panels}&2&4&6&8\\\hline\text{Lights}&44&88&132&172\end{array}$?

options.why: Adds $2$ and $22$ instead of multiplying two panels by lights per panel.
Adds $4$ panels to $22$ lights per panel instead of multiplying them.
Drops the carried ten when calculating $6 \times 22$, producing $122$ instead of $132$.
